To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of upsampling layers is crucial for obtaining good results; (2) the performance of OnAVOS can be improved by combining the predictions for multiple objects; and (3) OnAVOS performs better than a state-of-the-art method for single object segmentation.
the combination of the predictions of multiple OnAVOS runs is an effective way to handle multiple objects in videos, and that upsampling layers can improve the segmentation quality.
(a) our method is robust to the number of objects, (b) it is robust to the object size, and (c) the upsampling layers are crucial to achieve a good segmentation performance.

the problem of video object segmentation, i.e. segmenting the pixels that belong to multiple objects in videos.

we were able to show that a single-object method can be extended to handle multiple objects and that the method is competitive to the state-of-the-art.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to achieve the state-of-the-art results for the DAVIS 2016 challenge with our OnAVOS method and that we are able, with a few extensions, to achieve the fifth place for the DAVIS2017 challenge.
we have successfully applied the OnAVOS method to the DAVIS dataset and that it has performed well.
we achieved the best performance on the DAVIS 2016 validation dataset, which is the best performance so far on a video object segmentation dataset.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple online learning approach can be competitive with state-of-the-art methods, even when using the same backbone networks.

a simple and efficient method, such as OnAVOS, can achieve good results on a complex task such as video object segmentation, when it is combined with a good pre-trained network and a good initialization of the network weights.
it is feasible to use a single network for multiple objects and that it is beneficial to use upsampling layers to increase the output resolution.
